title: Chippenham Stirling Memorial
crew_summary: 9 crew — 7 killed, 2 unknown fate including pilot Flt Sgt. John Whyte

external_narratives.summary: Imperial War Museums register entry for the Stirling Bomber BK784 crash site memorial at Chippenham, Cambridgeshire. A stone tablet set into the ground near the crash site on private farmland off Badlingham Road commemorates the seven crew who died on 23 May 1944.
key_details: Stone tablet on private farmland off Badlingham Road
Crew names: Aston, Eggbeer, McCrory, Pearce, Sharpen, Walley, Whyte

memorial_details:
Stone tablet set into the ground close to the crash site of a Short Stirling bomber aircraft. Incised inscription and names of crew members.

A stone tablet set into the ground near the crash site on private farmland off Badlingham Road commemorates the seven men who lost their lives.

A stone tablet set into the ground near the crash site on private farmland off Badlingham Road commemorates the seven men.
narrative: On 23 May 1944, Stirling BK784 of 90 Squadron, based at RAF Tuddenham, came down at Chippenham, Cambridgeshire. Seven crew members were killed: Flight Sergeant J. Whyte (pilot), R. Eggbeer, P. McCrory, B. Sharpen, and W.
inscription:
+ IN MEMORY OF
(7 NAMES)
CREW OF STIRLING BOMBER
BK 784
CRASHED HERE 23.5.1944
LEST WE FORGET
community_connection: The memorial is maintained by Chippenham Parish Council.
